title: Symmetry and periodicity of trig functions
keyIdea: Sine and cosine repeat every full turn, so sin(θ + 2π) = sin θ and cos(θ + 2π) = cos θ; their period is 2π. Tangent repeats every half-turn, so its period is π. On the unit circle, −θ is the mirror image of θ in the x-axis, which keeps x and flips y: cos(−θ) = cos θ (cosine is even) and sin(−θ) = −sin θ (sine is odd). The mirror in the y-axis gives π − θ, which keeps the height: sin(π − θ) = sin θ and cos(π − θ) = −cos θ. Symmetry finds the partner solution in one turn; the period finds the rest.

visual.caption: Is each identity true for every θ? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: slide a graph copy to find each period, mirror points to −θ and π − θ, sort identities, solve with symmetry and period.

kid: Turn a point once round the unit circle and it lands where it started. So sin and cos repeat every 2π. We say their period is 2π. Tan repeats sooner, every π.
Now turn the same angle the other way, to −θ. The new point is the mirror image in the x-axis. Its x is the same, so cos(−θ) = cos θ. Its y flips, so sin(−θ) = −sin θ.
Mirror the point in the y-axis instead. That gives the angle π − θ. The height does not change, so sin(π − θ) = sin θ. For example, sin(5π/6) = sin(π/6) = 1/2.
This is how you find every answer. To solve sin x = 1/2, start with x = π/6. The mirror gives 5π/6. Then add 2π to each one for every extra turn you need.
adult: Ages 16 to 18: A-level Pure Mathematics and the US standard F-TF.4, which asks students to use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions. The unit-circle definition makes each fact a picture rather than a rule to memorise.

A function f is periodic with period p if f(x + p) = f(x) for all x, and p is the smallest positive such number. A full turn returns the point to itself, so sine and cosine have period 2π (360°). A half-turn sends (x, y) to (−x, −y), which flips both but leaves y/x alone, so tangent has period π (180°). A function is even if f(−x) = f(x), so its graph is symmetric in the y-axis; it is odd if f(−x) = −f(x), so its graph has rotational symmetry about the origin. Cosine is even and sine is odd.

Common mistakes: writing cos(−θ) = −cos θ by treating the minus sign as if it always comes out; copying sin(π − θ) = sin θ to cos and missing the sign change, cos(π − θ) = −cos θ; giving tan a period of 2π, which is a period but not the smallest; reading sin(θ + 2π) as sin θ + 2π; and stopping at the calculator value when solving, which misses the partner from symmetry and every solution from the period. Careful with ranges: count every turn the interval covers.

In the lab you slide a dashed copy of each graph until it fits to find three periods, place Q at −θ and at π − θ for four angles each, and sort seven identities as always true or not. Then you tap every solution of four equations on their graphs, the last over two full turns.

practice.hint: 5π/6 = π − π/6. What does the mirror in the y-axis do to the height?
practice.explain: sin(π − θ) = sin θ, so sin(5π/6) = sin(π/6) = 1/2. The mirror in the y-axis keeps the height.

practice.prompt: θ = {a}°. Which angle between 90° and 180° has the same sine as θ?
practice.hint: Use sin(180° − θ) = sin θ: mirror the point in the y-axis.
practice.explain: sin(180° − θ) = sin θ, so the angle is 180° − {a}° = {=180-a}°.

practice.prompt: Which is true for every θ?
practice.hint: −θ is the mirror image in the x-axis. Which coordinate stays the same?
practice.explain: The mirror in the x-axis keeps x, so cos(−θ) = cos θ: cosine is even. It flips y, so sin(−θ) = −sin θ.

practice.prompt: How many solutions has sin x = 1/2 for 0 ≤ x ≤ {n}·2π?
practice.hint: Find the two solutions in one turn, then count the turns.
practice.explain: Each full turn gives two solutions (π/6 and 5π/6, plus 2π each turn). {n} turns give {=2*n} solutions.

practice.prompt: What is the period of y = tan x?
practice.hint: A half-turn flips both x and y. What happens to y/x?
practice.explain: tan(x + π) = tan x because a half-turn flips both coordinates and leaves y/x alone. 2π also works but is not the smallest.

pool.prompt: Which describes the graph of y = cos x?
choices: symmetric in the y-axis, because cosine is even
rotational symmetry about the origin, because cosine is odd
pool.explain: cos(−x) = cos x, so cosine is even and its graph is a mirror image in the y-axis.

pool.hint: π − θ is the mirror in the y-axis. What happens to x?
pool.explain: The mirror in the y-axis flips x, so cos(π − θ) = −cos θ.

pool.prompt: One solution of cos x = c is x = {a}°. What is the next solution above 360° that comes from the period alone?
pool.explain: cos(x + 360°) = cos x, so {a}° + 360° = {=a+360}° is also a solution.

pool.hint: Adding 2π inside the bracket is a full turn.
pool.explain: A full turn lands on the same point, so sin(θ + 2π) = sin θ.

pool.prompt: How many solutions has tan x = 1 for 0 ≤ x < {n}π?
pool.hint: tan has period π, and there is one solution in each interval of length π.
pool.explain: x = π/4 + kπ, one in each interval of length π, so there are {=n} solutions in 0 ≤ x < {n}π.

pool.prompt: Which pair of angles in 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π solves cos x = −1/2?
pool.hint: Cosine is negative on the left. cos(2π − θ) = cos θ gives the partner.
pool.explain: cos(2π/3) = −1/2. The mirror in the x-axis keeps x, so 2π − 2π/3 = 4π/3 also works.

pool.hint: Sine is odd: what does the minus sign do?

pool.prompt: Why does tan have period π when sin and cos have period 2π?
choices: A half-turn flips both sin and cos, so their ratio is unchanged.
tan grows twice as fast as sin.
tan is only defined up to π.
pool.hint: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ. What does a half-turn do to each?
pool.explain: sin(θ + π) = −sin θ and cos(θ + π) = −cos θ, so the ratio sin/cos is the same.

pool.prompt: sin x = 0.4 has a solution x = α between 0 and π/2. Which other solution lies in 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π?
pool.hint: Same sine means the same height.
pool.explain: sin(π − α) = sin α, the mirror in the y-axis. −α and π + α give −0.4.
